definition: A man who is unable to find a sexual or romantic partner despite wanting one, often associated with online communities marked by resentment and misogyny.
notes: Coined 1997 by a Canadian woman; reclaimed and politicized by male communities post-2010; associated with radicalization and several mass-casualty events.

definition: A man who pursues casual sex while being emotionally unavailable, dishonest, or manipulative toward partners.
notes: Rose to prominence circa 2014–2016 via social media; also spelled fuckboi; older prison slang meaning differed (a submissive male used sexually by others).

definition: Abbreviated form of fuckboy; a sexually exploitative and emotionally irresponsible man.
notes: Sanitized abbreviation enabling use in censored or broadcast contexts; shares concept slug with fuckboy.

definition: A sexually permissive person, typically a woman; used as an insult but partially reclaimed in AAVE and hip-hop culture.
notes: AAVE origin; pervasive in hip-hop since 1990s; increasingly gender-neutral in internet usage; phonetic respelling of whore but treated as a distinct lexical item.

definition: To have sex with someone, typically implying a casual or vigorous encounter.
notes: Popularized by the smash-or-pass meme format; crude level is moderate — blunt but not anatomical; also used in gaming contexts with no sexual meaning.

definition: To send a private message to someone on social media with romantic or sexual intent, often after publicly engaging with their content.
notes: DMs = direct messages; peaked approximately 2016–2017 on Twitter and Instagram; still understood but now slightly dated as a novel phrase.

definition: The male anus framed as a penetrable orifice; portmanteau of boy and pussy, originating in AAVE and gay male communities.
notes: Primarily used in gay male and queer contexts; spread to broader internet culture via meme communities; carries playful rather than purely pejorative tone.

definition: To ejaculate (verb) or semen (noun); originating in AAVE and widely adopted across hip-hop and internet slang.
notes: AAVE origin; polysemous (nuts = testicles in a separate, milder usage); extremely common in online sexual discourse and explicit music lyrics.

definition: Not Safe For Work; a content warning tag indicating sexually explicit, graphic, or otherwise inappropriate material.
notes: Originated in early internet and forum culture circa early 2000s; near-universal across English-speaking internet; antonym SFW (safe for work) also common.

definition: A deliberately sexualized photo or video posted on social media to attract desire, attention, or validation from viewers.
notes: Requires knowledge of thirsty (sexually desirous sense) to fully decode; became mainstream Instagram and TikTok vocabulary circa 2018–2020.

definition: Desperately eager for sexual or romantic attention in a way that reads as needy or off-putting.
notes: Semantic shift extending the physical-thirst metaphor; widely understood across age groups; can be self-deprecating or critical depending on context.

definition: To receive far more replies than likes on a social media post, signaling community rejection; deployed in sexual shaming contexts when someone's behavior or hypocrisy is publicly condemned.
notes: Not inherently sexual; included for its role in online sexual shaming dynamics; peaked on Twitter circa 2020–2021; recognition drops sharply among non-Twitter users.

definition: To publicly reveal someone's sexual images, messages, or behavior without their consent, typically as retaliation or shaming.
notes: Verbal form; closely linked to leaked nudes and revenge porn phenomena; used as a threat in phrases like I will expose you; also used in non-sexual scandal contexts.

definition: Nude or sexually explicit photographs or videos of a person distributed without that person's consent.
notes: Focuses on content and mechanism (the leak); gained mainstream prominence after the 2014 celebrity iCloud breach; shares concept slug with revenge porn, which emphasizes perpetrator motive.

definition: The non-consensual distribution of intimate or sexually explicit images of a person, typically by a former partner as retaliation.
notes: Now a legal term in many jurisdictions; preferred clinical term is non-consensual intimate image sharing (NCII); shares concept slug with leaked nudes.

definition: To create a false online identity in order to deceive someone into a romantic or sexual relationship.
notes: Popularized by the 2010 documentary and subsequent MTV series; motivations include sexual access, emotional manipulation, or financial fraud; used as both verb and noun.

definition: The act of abruptly cutting off all communication with a romantic or sexual partner without explanation.
notes: Mainstream enough to appear in major dictionaries; strongly associated with dating app culture; also used in platonic and professional contexts, diluting the sexual specificity.

definition: The practice of sending intermittent flirtatious or affectionate signals to someone without any intention of committing to a relationship.
notes: Metaphor from the Hansel and Gretel breadcrumb trail; popularized in dating advice media circa 2017; less mainstream than ghosting; recognition concentrated among active dating-app users.

definition: An undefined romantic or sexual relationship that has the qualities of a committed partnership but lacks explicit labels or mutual commitment.
notes: Portmanteau of situation and relationship; popularized on TikTok circa 2021–2023; fills a genuine lexical gap for ambiguous modern relationship structures that predate the term.

definition: A relationship between two friends who engage in sexual activity without romantic commitment or exclusivity.
notes: Sufficiently mainstream to title two major Hollywood films (2011); euphemistic in that benefits is a coded reference to sex; widely understood across generations and regions.

definition: Abbreviation for friends with benefits; a sexual relationship between friends without romantic commitment.
notes: Primarily used in dating app bios, personal ads, and online forums; shares concept slug with full form.

definition: Abbreviation for one-night stand; a single sexual encounter with no expectation of ongoing contact.
notes: Somewhat more common in UK English dating contexts and personal ads than in American usage; shares concept slug with one-night stand.

definition: A sexual encounter between two people spanning a single occasion with no intention of meeting again for sex.
notes: Decades-old idiom with theatrical origin (a one-night performance stop on a tour); mainstream and widely used across all English-speaking regions.

definition: A social pattern, particularly among young adults and on college campuses, characterized by casual sexual encounters without expectation of commitment.
notes: Used analytically in academic sociology as well as popular discourse; hookup alone refers to a specific encounter while hookup culture describes the broader norm.

definition: A sexual arrangement in which both parties agree there is no emotional commitment, exclusivity, or expectation of a continuing relationship.
notes: General idiom applied to many non-sexual contexts (gifts, business deals) but immediately understood in sexual contexts; abbreviated NSA in personal ads; also a 2011 film title.
